**STEP 1 - Scene:** An airline-style tray meal with four components: glazed chicken pieces, sliced roast beef, a fruit cup, and a green leafy salad, plus a glass of water (not counted).

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** The beef sits on a side plate of about 20 cm (area ≈ 314 cm²). The chicken plate is similar. The fruit and salad are in bowls of about 15 cm (area ≈ 177 cm²). I estimate each item against its own vessel.

**STEP 3 - Items:** Glazed chicken pieces in a sweet orange sauce; sliced roast beef; mixed fruit (strawberry, melon, pineapple); spinach or arugula with small tomato pieces. No separate dressing is clearly visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:**
- Beef: ~30% of the 20 cm plate (≈94 cm²)
- Chicken: ~45% of the 20 cm plate (≈141 cm²)
- Fruit: ~70% of the 15 cm bowl (≈124 cm²)
- Salad: ~70% of the 15 cm bowl (≈124 cm²)

**STEP 5 - Volume:**
- Beef: 94 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 141 ml
- Chicken: 141 cm² × 1.0 cm ≈ 141 ml
- Fruit: 124 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 372 ml
- Salad: 124 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 372 ml

**STEP 6 - Grams:**
- Beef: 141 ml × 0.9 ≈ 127 g
- Chicken: 141 ml × 0.9 ≈ 127 g
- Fruit: 372 ml × 0.5 ≈ 186 g
- Salad: 372 ml × 0.15 ≈ 56 g

**STEP 7 - Energy:**
- Beef: 127 g × 220 kcal/100 g ≈ 279 kcal
- Chicken: 127 g × 220 kcal/100 g ≈ 279 kcal (glazed, so I use a similar value)
- Fruit: 186 g × 50 kcal/100 g ≈ 93 kcal
- Salad: 56 g × 20 kcal/100 g ≈ 11 kcal

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** The total is about 500 g of food and about 660 kcal. That is plausible for a full airline main course with fruit and salad. The chicken figure has the most uncertainty because the glaze and portion depth are hard to judge from above.

Total: about 510 g, about 665 kcal.
